problem: End-to-end latent memories of navigation agents are trained only through the downstream task signal, so they keep only reactive information and transfer poorly (sim2real, sensor noise), while explicit reconstruction spends capacity on unneeded precision and is brittle under noise.
motivation: Simulated PointGoal agents reach ~99% success but fall far short in real environments, and classical map+plan stacks stay competitive. The authors argue a representation should be optimized for usability rather than reconstruction fidelity, and that behavior cloning lets the agent take memory-less (reactive) shortcuts instead of integrating history into a latent map.
key_idea: Learn the agent's latent memory by having a blind auxiliary agent (the 'mole') use it as its only input to navigate to many nearby subgoals branching out from waypoints, with no reconstruction loss (the 'Navigability' loss).
insight: Blindness removes the reactive shortcut, so the aux agent's behavior-cloning loss can only be met by a memory that encodes navigable space, and gradients travel a longer chain through the memory. Ablations show that (e) Navig.+BC beats plain BC on the same long+short data (c) mainly under noise (90.9 vs 89.6 Succ; 73.3 vs 74.0 SPL in NoisySim, though the gap is larger in the robot test). The reconstruction-supervised variant (h) is good in clean sim (94.9 Succ) but collapses in NoisySim (76.7). Probing shows Navigability gives lower IoU than PPO (19.8 vs 31.0) but much better navigation on the decoded map (Sym-SPL 14.7 vs 10.1; NoisySim 13.2 vs 6.1), so it optimizes navigability rather than reconstruction.
method: Navigability loss: the main agent's GRU state r_t is passed to a blind aux GRU policy rho (with only subgoal vector and previous action as input), trained by cross-entropy behavior cloning on shortest-path actions to a batch of subgoals; gradients flow back into the representation.

Long/short episode structure: standard PointGoal episodes are long episodes; waypoints are sampled every 3 m and 20 subgoals are attached to each at Euclidean distance 3-5 m, giving ~36M short episodes.
Subgoal mining: subgoals with geodesic/Euclidean ratio < T=1.5 are discarded, because following the compass would suffice for them.
Hybrid Navig.+BC training: the main policy is also behavior-cloned on long episodes while the aux loss runs on short ones, so the observations gathered on short episodes are not wasted.

Two-phase training: 50M steps of pre-training (PPO / BC / Navigability / reconstruction variants), then the main policy is re-initialized and PPO-finetuned for 50M steps on PointGoal without the aux agent (100M steps total).

Communication ablation: r is fed to rho as an input at each step (e.1), used as the initial hidden state (e.2, default), or as initial state with 128 extra dimensions (e.3). Hidden-state continuity across teleports is also ablated.
Probing with Sym-SPL: a decoder predicts a 95x95 ego-centric occupancy map from r; a new Symmetric-SPL metric measures navigation quality on the predicted map versus the GT map.

setting.backbone: half-width 4-channel ResNet18 + GRU-512 main agent, with an auxiliary GRU blind policy (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: Gibson (72 train scenes) in Habitat; 100M env steps total (50M pretraining + 50M PPO finetuning) plus ~36M generated short episodes (only ~5% of visual observations are seen in the Navigability-only variant)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + GPS/compass pointgoal + previous action
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: FORWARD 25cm / TURN_LEFT 10° / TURN_RIGHT 10° / STOP (mapped to open-loop velocity commands on the robot)
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson); real Locobot in an office building
setting.privileged: Simulator ground-truth shortest paths and maps are used in training only (for aux-agent BC labels and probing); none at test time.

numbers.method: (e) Navig. + BC◻ (Navigability + BC, then PPO finetune), noiseless Sim
numbers.extra: 100M env steps total; no training noise

numbers_note: Only PointGoal on Gibson (sim and noisy sim) and 11 real-robot episodes are reported; the real-robot benchmark has no canonical name. Test-split evaluation is on the standard Gibson test episodes.
results: Navigability+BC (e) reaches 95.5 Succ / 80.3 SPL in sim and 90.9 / 73.3 in NoisySim, against PPO's 89.6/71.7 and 74.6/55.8 and BC data-aug (c)'s 94.2/80.1 and 89.6/74.0. On a real Locobot with 11 episodes it gets 81.8 Succ / 45.6 SPL, versus 72.7/36.3 for BC, 45.5/14.7 for PPO and 36.4/29.6 for a map+plan baseline. In clean sim the classical planner is better (95.7/89.9), but in noise it collapses to 27.9/16.3.
limitations: Real-robot evaluation has only 11 episodes and a single environment, so the sim2real evidence is statistically weak.
Only PointGoal was tested, and the gains over BC with data augmentation in NoisySim are small; the SPL in sim is not better than pure BC or reconstruction (h).
Training needs privileged simulator shortest paths and a large amount of short-episode data, and the results are sensitive to design choices (hidden-state continuity, the communication mode).
